plannedR1.prompt:
Repaint the attached grey block-out as ONE finished building sprite for a pastoral isometric railway game.

Style: that of the attached style board. Crisp pixel-art-inspired clustered shading, broad readable masses, three or four shades per material, restrained detail, a strong silhouette. The palette family of the whole game: forest green #294638, moss #78804C, oat cream #E4D5B5, limestone #BCA98B, slate #626B6C, teal #477B82, copper #A36B42. Light from the upper left: roofs and tops lightest, lower-left walls mid, lower-right walls darkest.

Camera: keep the block-out's camera exactly. Orthographic 2:1 isometric, ground edges two pixels across for each pixel down, vertical edges vertical, no perspective. Do not rotate or tilt the view. The foot of the lower-left wall runs parallel to the plinth's lower-left edge and the foot of the lower-right wall parallel to its lower-right edge: both walls equally steep, neither flatter than the block-out's. Do not turn the building towards the viewer: the lower-right wall is seen as much from the side as the lower-left wall. Show the whole building with a clear margin all round: nothing touches the edge of the picture.

Footprint: the grey plinth is the building's footprint. The building stands on it and fills it: its outer walls rise from the plinth's edges, and at ground level nothing reaches outside the plinth. Keep the foot of the two visible walls plain and straight from corner to corner, so that it shows where the building stands: no bushes, crates, steps or loose objects in front of it. Above the ground the shape is free: roofs, towers, chimneys and machinery may differ from the block and may overhang a little. The dark openings in the block-out show where the front door, or a depot's train portals, are; keep them in those walls.

Do not paint the plinth itself: no ground, floor slab, pavement, grass or shadow under or around the building. A real RGBA PNG with a transparent background (alpha zero) and opaque building surfaces.

Never: rails, trains, people, vehicles, smoke, lettering, signs with text, borders, glow, or loose objects standing apart from the building.

View r1: The building is turned a quarter turn clockwise seen from above. The front faces the upper left, away from the camera, and nothing of it is in this picture: no entrance door and none of the front's windows or other features on either visible wall. The lower-left wall is the right-hand side; the lower-right wall is the BACK, plainer than the front.

Diesel age: larger and more industrial, still of the same countryside. Warm brick walls on cream stone bases, riveted iron and steel trusses, slate or corrugated roofs with roof lights, big sliding doors, iron cranes and tanks, forest-green paint.

Fuel Pump. A railway refuelling point for diesel engines.
What r0 shows; carry it round the building: a SQUARE red-brick pump house on cream limestone quoins and base; on it, a riveted forest-green steel tank with two oat-cream bands, lying on a dark steel frame, its long axis parallel to the front; a small slate-roofed gable over the door; the door, forest-green planks, in the middle of the front wall; a tall forest-green hose crane whose post stands at the front's left corner (in r0, the left corner of the picture), whose jib reaches out over the front, past its edge, high above train height, with a hose hanging from its end; pipes from the tank to the crane, with copper bands. Carry round the tank's manhole, top pipe, end vent, rivets and frame, as in the master. The square house has one front door only.

r1: the front faces the upper left, out of sight. The lower-left wall is the right-hand side: r0's lower-right wall, copied as it stands. The crane's post stands at the far (top) corner, behind the building. Its jib reaches away to the upper left, over the hidden front, high up.
